_comment: Static filter metadata overlay — prose, genre, and notes only. Keys are engine-reported names (join by name at runtime; engine enumerations are sole authority for names/IDs/order — architecture §2). Structural facets are NOT stored here: quality/focus/ratio ship live in FiltersItem descriptions, apodizing in arg bit 0, phase is the name token (-lp/-mp/-ip) where present, else a manual-derived phase key on the entry; filters the taxonomy does not fit carry none. Genre comes from the manual's own genre column (not editorial).
_join_rules: 1) Exact name match. 2) On miss, apply aliases. 3) On miss with a '-2s' suffix, strip the suffix, join the base entry, and append two_stage_note to the description. 4) Still no match → render engine name without description (architecture §2). 5) An entry flagged sdm_two_stage gets sdm_two_stage_note inserted after its description, but only where the joining control sits on the SDM chain (store/schema.js desc 'sdm_filter'); the PCM chain omits it. Unrelated to two_stage_note, which is keyed by the '-2s' name and comes last.
two_stage_note: Two stage oversampling: the first stage rate conversion is performed by at least a factor of 8 using the selected algorithm, then the signal is further converted to the final rate using an algorithm optimized for content already processed to at least 8x rate. This lowers overall CPU load while preserving the same conversion quality. Especially useful for the highest output rates.
sdm_two_stage_note: Processing is two stages with a minimum 16x intermediate rate.

guidance.1x_vs_nx: Filter selection for 1x rates covers source sampling rates below 50 kHz (base rates); Nx covers everything above.
guidance.apodizing: An apodizing filter should be used at least when the Apod counter increments higher than 10 during any single track. 'Only suitable for highest technical quality source materials' means material where the Apod counter stays below 10 for the entire track.
guidance.quality_ratings: Quality ratings are not absolute, but a relative guidance regarding technical quality of filter's output vs other filters in the list.
guidance.author_recommendation: Different variants of poly-sinc are the most recommended by the author.

length.tradeoff: Frequency-domain accuracy against time-domain compactness. Longer filters buy sharper roll-off and higher stop-band attenuation at the cost of longer pre- and post-ringing; shorter filters ring less but roll off slower and attenuate less.
length.mechanism: Manual §4.6 states the trade in both directions: short variants have 'shorter pre- and post-ringings at the expense of filtering quality (not as sharp roll-off)'; long variants have 'longer pre- and post-ringings with improved filtering quality (faster roll-off)'.
symptoms_pointing_shorter: softened or smeared attacks on percussive or electronic material
transient character described as blunted or slow
symptoms_pointing_longer: top-octave texture described as coarse or grainy on dense material
loss of fine timbre detail on well-recorded acoustic material
length.contested: The ringing a length change moves sits at or near Nyquist, where audibility is small and contested. The mechanism is real; the effect size on 44.1 kHz material is disputed and shrinks further at higher source rates.

phase.tradeoff: Where the filter's ringing energy sits in time. Linear phase places it symmetrically around a transient, so energy arrives before the attack (pre-ringing); minimum phase moves all of it after the attack at the cost of frequency-dependent group delay; intermediate phase splits the difference with small pre-ringing and longer post-ringing.
phase.mechanism: Manual §4.6: minimum phase variants have 'no pre-ringing, but somewhat long post-ringing'; linear phase variants have symmetric pre- and post-ringing; intermediate phase variants have 'small pre-ringing and longer post-ringing'. Phase is encoded in the filter name (-lp/-ip/-mp).
symptoms_pointing_minimum: pre-echo or a soft leading edge on strong transients, studio multi-track material
symptoms_pointing_linear: spatial impression on material recorded in a real acoustic environment — the manual's 'space' focus spans linear, intermediate and minimum phase variants
phase.contested: No published discrimination test of minimum versus linear phase resampling exists (PHASE.md §10); adjacent group-delay audibility thresholds suggest small effects. State the mechanism, never a guaranteed audible difference.

apodizing.tradeoff: Whether the filter also cleans up ringing already baked into the source by its original ADC or mastering decimation filter. Non-apodizing filters pass those artifacts through; the manual marks the half-band variants (poly-sinc-hb, -hb-xs, -hb-s, -hb-m, -hb-l, poly-sinc-gauss-halfband, -halfband-s) and poly-sinc-ext2-xl as 'only suitable for highest technical quality source materials'.
apodizing.mechanism: Manual §4.6: an apodizing filter should be used at least when the Apod counter increments past 10 during any single track. The counter is the objective per-track signal — read it rather than guessing from genre or provenance.
symptoms_pointing_apodizing: hardness or glare present on some recordings and absent on others of the same kind — source-dependent, which EQ cannot fix without penalising the clean recordings
apodizing.contested: Benefit depends entirely on the source's own mastering chain; on clean sources apodizing and non-apodizing variants converge. The Apod counter, not listening impressions, is the decision signal.

guidance.one_axis_at_a_time: A filter suggestion holds every other axis fixed and moves one — length, phase, or apodizing, never several at once. Moving two axes together makes the A/B unattributable and teaches nothing.
negative_rules: Midrange tonality, nasality, boom, mud and sibilance are EQ symptoms, never filter symptoms. A filter recommendation for any of these is a confident non-answer.
EQ bands cannot pre-ring: any pre-echo in the chain comes from the oversampling filter alone (PHASE.md §1, §9). Never migrate a filter-phase explanation onto an EQ band or vice versa.
Filter axes plausibly touch only: transient character, top-octave texture, spatial diffuseness, and source-dependent hardness. A complaint outside those regions does not get a filter recommendation.
A phase or group-delay story must never become the escape hatch for a complaint the model cannot otherwise fix (PHASE.md §9).

none.description: No sample rate conversion happens. Only sample depth is changed as needed.

IIR.description: Analog-sounding filter especially suitable for recordings containing strong transients, with long post-ringing as a side effect (not usually audible due to masking). A really steep IIR filter is used. This filter type is similar to analog filters and has no pre-ringing but long post-ringing. Small amount of passband ripple is also present. Medium attenuation. IIR filter is applied in the time domain.

IIR2.description: Analog-sounding filter especially suitable for recordings containing strong transients, with long post-ringing as a side effect (not usually audible due to masking). A steep IIR filter is used. This filter type is similar to analog filters and has no pre-ringing but long post-ringing. Medium attenuation. No passband ripple. IIR filter is applied in the time domain.

FIR.description: Typical "oversampling" digital filter, generally suitable for most uses (slight pre- and post-ringing), but best on classical music recorded in a real-world acoustic environment such as a concert hall. This is the most ordinary filter type, usually present in hardware. This filter is applied in the time domain. Average amount of pre- and post-ringing.

asymFIR.description: Asymmetric FIR, good for jazz/blues and other music containing transients recorded in a real-world acoustic environment. Otherwise same as FIR, but with shorter pre-ringing and longer post-ringing. Modifies phase response, but not as much as minimum phase FIR.

minphaseFIR.description: Minimum phase FIR, good for pop/rock/electronic music containing strong transients such as drums and percussion, where the recording is made in a studio using multi-track equipment. No pre-ringing, but somewhat long post-ringing.

FFT.description: Technically good steep "brickwall" filter, but might have some side effects (pre-ringing) on material containing strong transients. This filter is similar to FIR, but it is applied in the frequency domain and is quite efficient from a performance point of view while having a rather long impulse response. The length of this filter can be configured separately in the FFT filter length setting.

poly-sinc-lp.description: Linear phase polyphase sinc filter. Very high quality linear phase resampling filter that can perform most of the typical conversion ratios. Good phase response, but has some amount of pre-ringing. See "FIR" for further details.

poly-sinc-mp.description: Minimum phase polyphase sinc filter, otherwise similar to poly-sinc. Altered phase response, but no pre-ringing. See minphaseFIR for further details.

poly-sinc-short-lp.description: Otherwise similar to poly-sinc, but shorter pre- and post-ringing at the expense of filtering quality (not as sharp roll-off).

poly-sinc-short-mp.description: Minimum phase variant of poly-sinc-short. Otherwise similar to poly-sinc-mp, but shorter post-ringing. Most optimal transient reproduction.

poly-sinc-long-lp.description: Otherwise similar to poly-sinc, but longer pre- and post-ringing with improved filtering quality (faster roll-off).

poly-sinc-long-ip.description: Intermediate phase version of poly-sinc-long, with small pre-ringing and longer post-ringing, and improved filtering quality (faster roll-off).

poly-sinc-long-mp.description: Minimum phase variant of poly-sinc-long. Otherwise similar to poly-sinc-mp, but longer post-ringing with improved filtering quality (faster roll-off).

poly-sinc-hb.description: Linear phase polyphase half-band filter with steep roll-off and high attenuation.
poly-sinc-hb.notes: Only suitable for highest technical quality source materials.

poly-sinc-hb-xs.description: Extremely short linear phase polyphase half-band filter with slow roll-off and low attenuation.
poly-sinc-hb-xs.notes: Only suitable for highest technical quality source materials.

poly-sinc-hb-s.description: Short linear phase polyphase half-band filter with slow roll-off and average attenuation.
poly-sinc-hb-s.notes: Only suitable for highest technical quality source materials.

poly-sinc-hb-m.description: Medium linear phase polyphase half-band filter with average roll-off and medium attenuation.
poly-sinc-hb-m.notes: Only suitable for highest technical quality source materials.

poly-sinc-hb-l.description: Long linear phase polyphase half-band filter with fast roll-off and high attenuation.
poly-sinc-hb-l.notes: Only suitable for highest technical quality source materials.

poly-sinc-ext.description: Linear phase polyphase sinc filter with sharper roll-off and somewhat lower stop-band attenuation, while being roughly equal in length to poly-sinc.

poly-sinc-ext2.description: Linear phase polyphase sinc filter with sharp roll-off and high stop-band attenuation for extended frequency response, while completely cutting off by the Nyquist frequency. Optimal frequency response and harmonic structure.

poly-sinc-ext2-short.description: Linear phase polyphase sinc filter with slow roll-off and high stop-band attenuation for extended frequency response. Optimal frequency response and harmonic structure.

poly-sinc-ext2-medium.description: Linear phase polyphase sinc filter with fast roll-off and high stop-band attenuation for extended frequency response, while completely cutting off by the Nyquist frequency. Optimal frequency response and harmonic structure.

poly-sinc-ext2-long.description: Linear phase polyphase sinc filter with very fast roll-off and very high stop-band attenuation for extended frequency response, while completely cutting off by the Nyquist frequency. Optimal frequency response and harmonic structure.

poly-sinc-ext2-xla.description: Very steep 8x longer version of poly-sinc-ext2-long.

poly-sinc-ext2-xl.description: Very steep 8x longer non-apodizing version of poly-sinc-ext2-long.
poly-sinc-ext2-xl.notes: Only suitable for highest technical quality source materials.

poly-sinc-ext2-hires-lp.description: Linear phase polyphase sinc filter for hi-res content, with very high stop-band attenuation. Also suitable for playback of lossy compression such as MP3 or MQA.

poly-sinc-ext2-hires-ip.description: Intermediate phase polyphase sinc filter for hi-res content, with very high stop-band attenuation. Also suitable for playback of lossy compression such as MP3 or MQA.

poly-sinc-ext2-hires-mp.description: Minimum phase polyphase sinc filter for hi-res content, with very high stop-band attenuation. Also suitable for playback of lossy compression such as MP3 or MQA.

poly-sinc-mqa/mp3-lp.description: Linear phase polyphase sinc filter optimized for playing back MQA- or MP3-encoded content in order to clean up high frequency noise added by the MQA or MP3 encoding. Also suitable for upsampling PCM sources of ≥ 88.2 kHz sampling rate, especially for hi-res PCM recordings of ≥ 176.4 kHz sampling rate. Very short ringing. Early slow roll-off.

poly-sinc-xtr-lp.description: Linear phase polyphase sinc filter with extreme roll-off and attenuation.

poly-sinc-xtr-mp.description: Minimum phase polyphase sinc filter with extreme roll-off and attenuation.

poly-sinc-xtr-short-lp.description: Short linear phase polyphase sinc filter with extreme roll-off and attenuation.

poly-sinc-xtr-short-mp.description: Short minimum phase polyphase sinc filter with extreme roll-off and attenuation.

poly-sinc-gauss-short.description: Short Gaussian polyphase sinc filter. Optimal time-frequency response.

poly-sinc-gauss-medium.description: Gaussian polyphase sinc filter. Optimal time-frequency response.

poly-sinc-gauss-long.description: Long Gaussian polyphase sinc filter with extremely high attenuation. Optimal time-frequency response.

poly-sinc-gauss-xla.description: Apodizing extra long Gaussian polyphase sinc filter with extremely high attenuation. Optimal time-frequency response.

poly-sinc-gauss-xl.description: Extra long Gaussian polyphase sinc filter with extremely high attenuation. Optimal time-frequency response.

poly-sinc-gauss-hires-lp.description: Linear phase Gaussian filter for hi-res content with extremely high attenuation. Optimal time-frequency response. Also suitable for playback of lossy compression such as MP3 or MQA.

poly-sinc-gauss-hires-ip.description: Intermediate phase Gaussian filter for hi-res content with extremely high attenuation. Optimal time-frequency response. Also suitable for playback of lossy compression such as MP3 or MQA.

poly-sinc-gauss-hires-mp.description: Minimum phase Gaussian filter for hi-res content with extremely high attenuation. Optimal time-frequency response. Also suitable for playback of lossy compression such as MP3 or MQA.

poly-sinc-gauss-halfband.description: Linear phase half-band Gaussian filter. Slightly leaky around Nyquist, but extremely high attenuation.
poly-sinc-gauss-halfband.notes: Only suitable for highest technical quality source materials.

poly-sinc-gauss-halfband-s.description: Short linear phase half-band Gaussian filter. Leaky around Nyquist, but high attenuation.
poly-sinc-gauss-halfband-s.notes: Only suitable for highest technical quality source materials.

ASRC.description: Special type of filter, slightly similar to FIR, but with a possibility of asynchronous operation for conversions from any rate to any other rate. Computationally heavy.

polynomial-1.description: Polynomial interpolation. No apparent pre- or post-ringing. Frequency response rolls off slowly in the top octave. Poor stop-band rejection and will thus leak a fairly high amount of ultrasonic distortion. These types of filters are sometimes referred to as "non-ringing" by some manufacturers.

polynomial-2.description: Similar to polynomial-1, but higher stop-band rejection and only one cycle of pre- and post-ringing.

minringFIR-lp.description: Minimum ringing FIR. Uses a special algorithm to create a linear phase filter that minimizes ringing while providing better frequency response and attenuation than polynomial interpolators. Performance and ringing between polynomial and poly-sinc-short.

closed-form.description: Closed form interpolation with a high number of taps.

closed-form-fast.description: Closed form interpolation with lower CPU load, but also lower precision. Output precision tuned to match about 24-bit PCM.

closed-form-M.description: Closed form interpolation with one million taps.

closed-form-16M.description: Closed form interpolation with 16 million taps.

sinc-S.description: Sinc filter with adaptive number of taps. Number of taps is 4096x conversion ratio. Very sharp roll-off and high attenuation. Variant of poly-sinc-ext2-xla.

sinc-M.description: Sinc filter with one million taps. Very sharp roll-off and high attenuation. Variant of poly-sinc-ext2-xla.

sinc-Mx.description: Constant time version of sinc-M. Filter length is constant in time, with one million taps at 16x PCM output rates. Variant of poly-sinc-ext2-xla. (65536x conversion ratio)

sinc-MG.description: Gaussian constant time filter with one million taps at 16x PCM output rates. Extremely high attenuation. Variant of poly-sinc-gauss-xl. (65536x conversion ratio)

sinc-MGa.description: Apodizing Gaussian constant time filter with one million taps at 16x PCM output rates. Extremely high attenuation. Variant of poly-sinc-gauss-xla. (65536x conversion ratio)

sinc-L.description: Sinc filter with adaptive number of taps. Number of taps is 131070x conversion ratio. Extremely sharp roll-off and average attenuation.

sinc-Ls.description: Average attenuation sinc filter with adaptive number of taps (4096x conversion ratio).

sinc-Lm.description: Average attenuation sinc filter with adaptive number of taps (16384x conversion ratio).

sinc-Ll.description: Average attenuation sinc filter with adaptive number of taps (65536x conversion ratio).

sinc-Lh.description: High attenuation sinc filter with adaptive number of taps (16384x ratio). Significantly better quality than sinc-L at 1/8th of the load.

sinc-short.description: Short average attenuation sinc filter with adaptive number of taps.

sinc-medium.description: Average attenuation sinc filter with adaptive number of taps.

sinc-long.description: Long average attenuation sinc filter with adaptive number of taps.

sinc-long-h.description: Long high attenuation sinc filter with adaptive number of taps.
